data.title: Ubisoft’s Q2 Bookings Beat Overshadowed by Deep Losses and Weak Guidance, Supporting a Hold
data.description:
In a report released on November 19, Aleksander Peterc from Bernstein maintained a Hold rating on UBISOFT Entertainment, with a price target of €4.00.

Aleksander Peterc gave his rating based on several factors, including Ubisoft’s modest second-quarter bookings beat, supported by Assassin’s Creed Black Flag Resynced and continued strength in key franchises. However, this was outweighed by a much larger-than-expected first-half operating loss and third-quarter bookings guidance that fell well below market expectations.
A full-year target remains achievable only if Ubisoft delivers an unusually strong fourth quarter, relying on unsigned partnerships, unreleased premium games and improved Rainbow Six Siege performance. Refinancing uncertainty and the possibility of further earnings downgrades add risk, but the heavily depressed share price already reflects significant concerns, supporting a balanced Hold view rather than a more negative recommendation.

In another report released on November 19, Barclays also maintained a Hold rating on the stock with a €4.75 price target.

data.title: Strong Q3 Momentum and Expanding Financing Potential Support Speculative Buy at $0.30 Target
data.description:
Analyst Noel Atkinson of Clarus reiterated a Buy rating on Ameritrust Financial Technologies, with a price target of $0.30.

Noel Atkinson’s rating is based on several factors supporting improving operating momentum. In Q3, lease originations rose 68% sequentially to $7.3 million, revenue increased 25% to $1.1 million, and the adjusted EBITDA loss was narrower than expected. Strong transaction values, minimal lease losses, and prime-credit customers also indicated disciplined underwriting.
The outlook strengthened further as application and approval activity accelerated in October, with the dealer network contributing more volume and better applicant screening. Atkinson also sees meaningful potential in used-car leasing and believes progress toward expanded financing capacity could support growth, leading him to maintain a speculative Buy rating and a $0.30 target price.

data.title: HireQuest: Buy Rating Maintained as Recovery Gains Momentum; Price Target Unchanged at $19
data.description:
In a report released today, Kevin Steinke from Barrington reiterated a Buy rating on HireQuest, with a price target of $19.00.

Kevin Steinke’s rating is based on HireQuest’s stronger-than-expected third-quarter performance and improving industry demand. Revenue and system-wide sales surpassed his estimates, while comparable revenue growth reached double digits after a difficult multi-year staffing environment. The acceleration from earlier quarters, including stronger weekly trends entering the fourth quarter, supports confidence that the recovery is gaining momentum.

Additional support comes from growth across HireQuest Direct and Snelling, stronger manufacturing staffing activity, and expanding opportunities through the national accounts program. The employee app is also helping franchisees recruit workers for assignments beyond their local markets, while the company’s compliance-focused placement process may benefit from tighter immigration enforcement. Given these catalysts and the improving outlook, Steinke maintained his Buy-equivalent rating and kept the price target unchanged at $19.

data.title: Intuit Rated Sell on Weak FY2027 Outlook and Rising AI Competition; Price Target Unchanged at $290
data.description:
In a report released on November 16, Billy Fitzsimmons from Piper Sandler maintained a Sell rating on Intuit, with a price target of $290.00.

Billy Fitzsimmons has given his Sell rating due to a combination of factors, beginning with Intuit’s weaker-than-expected fiscal 2027 revenue outlook, which implies a slower growth trajectory than the market had anticipated. He also sees meaningful near-term uncertainty as agentic search could pressure small-business software demand, potentially limiting QuickBooks momentum despite its recent price increases. The analyst believes the company is entering a transition period in which operating metrics may remain volatile.
Longer term, TurboTax faces rising competition, particularly after new AI products highlighted tax preparation as a potential use case, while consumer-focused AI agents could constrain Credit Karma’s recovery. Although the August QuickBooks pricing action should support first-quarter revenue and Intuit’s valuation is not excessive, Fitzsimmons views these benefits as insufficient to offset the execution and competitive risks. His price target remains unchanged at $290, reinforcing the cautious outlook.

Fitzsimmons covers the Technology sector, focusing on stocks such as Microsoft, Guidewire, and Intuit. According to TipRanks, Fitzsimmons has an average return of 8.9% and a 48.94% success rate on recommended stocks.

data.title: PMV Pharmaceuticals: Buy Rating Reaffirmed with Unchanged $5 Price Target Despite Competitive and Safety Concerns
data.description:
In a report released today, Robert Burns from H.C. Wainwright maintained a Buy rating on PMV Pharmaceuticals, with a price target of $5.00.

Robert Burns’s Buy rating is based on PMV Pharmaceuticals’ potential to remain competitive in the TP53 Y220C inhibitor market. He viewed updated rezatapopt results as less compelling because activity was concentrated in gynecologic cancers and appeared weaker in several other tumor types. The treatment also showed a less favorable safety profile, with more nausea and certain severe laboratory abnormalities reported.
Although cross-trial comparisons require caution, dalretapopt’s early results suggest that a broader and potentially better-tolerated rival could challenge rezatapopt. Burns also noted that PMVP shares had fallen about 33% from the session’s opening price, creating an attractive risk-reward opportunity if the company’s program executes well. His price target remains unchanged at $5, implying substantial upside from the cited $1.34 level.

According to TipRanks, Burns is a 4-star analyst with an average return of 9.8% and a 36.62% success rate. Burns covers the Healthcare sector, focusing on stocks such as PMV Pharmaceuticals, ArriVent BioPharma, Inc., and BlossomHill Therapeutics, Inc..
